title: 5% Yields: 'Whole System Collapses', What Happens To Markets | Gareth Soloway
speaker: Gareth Soloway

macro_themes.view: At ~5.3% the 10-year is basically at its near-term peak; expects a pullback below 5%.
Long term, 5%+ yields will break the economy; AI capex is masking the damage and it 'will end unbelievably badly', though not this year.
Diesel at all-time highs feeds into prices with a lag; inflation stays 3-4% for the foreseeable future.
Does not expect a hike in October given softer PCE and weak jobs.
Gridlock after the midterms has historically been bullish for stocks; oil rhetoric quieted ahead of the vote.
Would not buy a house at these yields; higher yields will drive house prices down.

calls.condition: Long-term 4%/3.5% only if a recession arrives.
calls.reason: Near-term peak: jobs data softening takes pressure off the Fed; in a recession yields might fall to 4% or 3.5% but not COVID levels as inflation stays sticky.
calls.quote: in the near term, we're basically there. I'm I am expecting a pullback that's going to be at least bringing us back below 5%.

calls.condition: Bullish while S&P holds above 7575; below it moves to neutral. Short-term target is a trend line ~1.4-1.75% higher (no number given), possibly before the midterms.
calls.reason: Six reasons (better PCE, strong growth data, best house on the block, earnings, earnings season, new-quarter inflows); orange trend line from 2022 ~1.4-1.75% above is the near-term target. Cautious for 2027 once AI capex slows.
calls.quote: I still think we're going 8,000 on the S&P by year end... anything above 7575 on the S&P, I remain bullish.

calls.condition: Above 87,200 -> 97,000; below 81,300 -> 75,500, and below that the 60s. Expects 100k within the next year.
calls.reason: Consolidating after bull-flag breakout; measured move to 97k if 87,200 breaks, but much near-term upside is in and it's overbought. Long-term gold and Bitcoin are the answer to fiscal irresponsibility.
calls.quote: It's got to get through this 87,200 level. If it does, there's a measured move to 97,000.

calls.condition: Bulls in charge while above the trend line (~4100); plans to load up on physical gold around 3500.
calls.reason: At a make-or-break trend line from May 2025; falling yields are saving it today. A break targets 3950 then 3500, a retest of the breakout level he calls a steal. Long-term target 13,000 by 2029-2031 on debt and money supply.
calls.quote: if we break below 4100, you go quickly to 3950. And if 3950... breaks, 3500 is the magic target.

calls.condition: If Hormuz and the Red Sea fully reopen to tankers, heads to the $60s, maybe $50s; otherwise oil sticks around 78.
calls.reason: Breakdown, retest of the broken trend line rejected; Iran rhetoric quieted before the midterms and tankers moving through Hormuz.
calls.quote: I'm anticipating further downside by the midterms. We should get down to this $78 per barrel level.

notes: Host states 'we're speaking on Tuesday, October 6th' (listing approx 2026-10-07). Recorded during/after the 2026-10-06 session (S&P new ATH 'today', gold 'up about 1% today'); marked intraday, could be after close. Oil price ~87 was said as 'back below 80 or down to about $87', taken as 87. 10y 'peak' framed as near-term pullback below 5%. Long-term ES bearish reflects 'cautious for 2027' and 'will end unbelievably badly'; he says not this year.
